title: Using Public Transportation
description: Learn to use buses and ask for directions
objectives: Ask which bus to take (Which bus goes to...?)
Ask for directions (How do I get to...?)
Understand basic direction words (take, go, stop)
Buy tickets and ask about fares

target_language.grammar_pattern:
Which + noun?
How do I + verb?
Does this + noun + verb?

Examples:
- Which bus goes to downtown?
- How do I get to the library?
- Does this bus go to Main Street?
- Get off at the next stop

grammar_patterns.label: Choosing options
examples: Which bus goes to downtown?
Which bus goes to the hospital?
Which train goes to the airport?

grammar_patterns.label: Asking for directions
examples: How do I get to the library?
How do I get to downtown?
How do I get to the mall?

grammar_patterns.label: Yes/No confirmation
examples: Does this bus go to Main Street?
Does this bus go to downtown?
Does this train go to the airport?

dialogue.speaker: You

dialogue.speaker: Person

speaking.title: Task 1: Ask about buses
speaking.instruction: Record yourself asking which bus goes to three places: the library, the hospital, and downtown.
speaking.example: Which bus goes to the library? Which bus goes to the hospital? Which bus goes to downtown?

speaking.title: Task 2: Bus conversation
speaking.instruction: Record a conversation where you ask someone how to get to the library by bus.
speaking.example:
You: Excuse me. How do I get to the library?
Person: Take bus 5.
You: Where do I get off?
Person: Get off at Main Street.
You: Thank you!

writing.title: Task 1: Write directions
writing.instruction: Someone asks you how to get to the hospital. Write 3-4 sentences giving them directions by bus.
writing.example: Take bus number 7. The bus goes to the hospital. Get off at Park Street. The hospital is there.

writing.title: Task 2: Write a bus conversation
writing.instruction: Write a conversation (8-10 lines) where you ask someone at the bus stop how to get to the mall.
writing.example:
You: Excuse me.
Person: Yes?
You: How do I get to the mall?
Person: Take bus 12.
You: Which stop?
Person: Get off at Oak Street.
You: How much is the fare?
Person: Two dollars.
You: Thank you!
Person: You're welcome.

sections.title: Question words: Which vs How
examples: Which bus goes to downtown? (asking to choose one option)
How do I get to downtown? (asking for the method/way)
sections.question: What's the difference between 'which' and 'how'?
sections.explanation: 'Which' asks you to choose from options (which bus, which stop). 'How' asks about the method or way to do something (how do I get there).

practice.sentence: ___ do I get to the library?

sections.title: Commands and instructions
examples: Take bus 5
Get off at Main Street
Go to the library
sections.question: How do we give directions and instructions?
sections.explanation: We use the base form of the verb (take, get, go) to give instructions. No 'I' or 'you' needed.

sections.title: Yes/No questions with 'does'
examples: Does this bus go to Main Street?
Does the bus stop here?
Does it cost money?
sections.question: How do we ask yes/no questions about things?
sections.explanation: We use 'does' to ask yes/no questions about things. Pattern: Does + [thing] + [verb]?

practice.sentence: ___ this bus go to the library?

sections.title: Asking About the Fare
examples: How much is the fare?
The fare is two dollars.
How much is a ticket?
Tickets are three dollars.
sections.question: How do we ask how much the bus costs?
sections.explanation: Use 'How much is + [thing]?' to ask the price, just like at a store. The answer is usually 'The fare is...' or 'It is...' plus a price.

quiz.question: You want to know which bus to take. What do you ask?
quiz.explanation: 'Which bus goes to downtown?' is the correct question.

quiz.question: You want to know how to get somewhere. What do you ask?
options: How do I get to the library?
quiz.explanation: 'How do I get to the library?' is correct. We use 'do I' in questions.

quiz.question: Someone tells you directions. They say 'Take bus 5'. What does 'take' mean?
options: Get on the bus / Use the bus
quiz.explanation: 'Take the bus' means 'get on the bus' or 'use the bus'. It's a common way to give transportation directions.

quiz.question: You want to confirm the bus goes to Main Street. What do you ask?
options: Does this bus go to Main Street?
quiz.explanation: 'Does this bus go to Main Street?' is the correct yes/no question.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: ___ bus goes to the hospital?
quiz.explanation: We use 'which' when choosing from options. 'Which bus' asks you to choose which one.

quiz.question: Someone says 'Get off at Park Street'. What does 'get off' mean?
options: Leave the bus / Exit the bus
quiz.explanation: 'Get off' means to leave or exit the bus. It's the opposite of 'get on'.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: How ___ I get to downtown?
quiz.explanation: We say 'How do I get to downtown?' Use 'do' with 'I' in questions.

quiz.question: Which is the MOST polite way to ask?
options: Excuse me, which bus goes to downtown?
quiz.explanation: 'Excuse me, which bus goes to downtown?' is the most polite. It starts with 'Excuse me' and uses a complete question.

quiz.question: Write a 6-line conversation where you ask someone at the bus stop how to get to the hospital.
quiz.explanation: Your conversation should include: getting attention politely, asking which bus, asking where to get off, and thanking them.

quiz.question: Where do you need to go by bus? Write the question you would ask: 'Which bus goes to ___?' or 'How do I get to ___?'
quiz.explanation: Practice with real places you need to go. This will help you remember the phrases.

somali.description: Baro sida basaska loo isticmaalo, jihooyinkana loo waydiisto
objectives: Waydii baska aad raacayso (Which bus goes to...?)
Waydii jihada (How do I get to...?)
Faham erayada jihada aasaasiga ah (take, go, stop)
Iibso tikidho oo waydii qiimaha safarka

sections.explanation: 'Which' wuxuu ku waydiinayaa inaad ikhtiyaarro ka dooratid (baska kee, joogsiga kee). 'How' wuxuu waydiinayaa habka ama sida loo sameeyo (sidee ku tagaa).
examples: Bas kee baa u tagaya xarunta magaalada? (waxaad weydiineysaa inaad doorato mid)
Sidee baan u tagaa xarunta magaalada? (waxaad weydiineysaa habka)

sections.explanation: Falka qaabkiisa aasaasiga ah (take, get, go) waxaan u isticmaalnaa tilmaan-bixinta. Uma baahnid 'I' ama 'you'.
examples: Raac baska 5
Ka deg waddada Main
Tag maktabadda

sections.explanation: 'does' waxaan u isticmaalnaa su'aalaha haa/maya ee waxyaabaha. Qaabka: Does + [shay] + [fal]?
examples: Baskani ma aadaa Main Street?
Basku ma halkan ku joogsadaa?
Ma lacag bay ku kacdaa?

sections.explanation: Isticmaal 'How much is + [thing]?' si aad u weydiiso qiimaha, sida dukaanka. Jawaabta badanaa waa 'The fare is...' ama 'It is...' iyo qiimo.
examples: Kirada waa imisa?
Kirada waa laba dollar.
Tigidh waa imisa?
Tigidho waa saddex dollar.

dialogue: Haa, waayahay. Maxaad u baahan tahay?
Waxaan u baahanahay inaan tago maktabadda. Bas kee ayaa maktabadda taga?
Fuul bas lambar 5. Wuxuu ku tagaa maktabadda.
Adaa mudan. Basku wuu imanayaa hadda.
